questions.explain: % gives the remainder after division. 4 goes into 23 five times (4 × 5 = 20), and 23 − 20 = 3, so 23 % 4 is 3.
why_wrong: 5 is 23 // 4, the quotient, not the remainder.
5.75 is 23 / 4, true division. % of two ints never has a fractional part.
20 is the part of 23 that 4 divides evenly (4 × 5), but % returns what is left over.

questions.q: Which expression is True exactly when the integer n is even?
questions.explain: An even number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2, and % gives that remainder. So n % 2 == 0 is True for 0, 2, 4, 8, … and False for every odd n.
why_wrong: A remainder of 1 means n is odd, so this is the test for odd numbers.
n / 2 is 0 only when n itself is 0. For n = 4 it is 2.0, so this is not an even test.
n // 2 == 0 is True only for n = 0 and n = 1, so it rejects 4 and accepts 1.

questions.q: Which of these expressions evaluates to False?
questions.explain: 3 > 2 is True, so and returns the right side, 2 > 5, which is False. The others are all True: not binds more loosely than >, so not 4 > 9 is not False, which is True; 17 % 5 is 2; and 0 or 5 > 1 returns 5 > 1, which is True.
why_wrong: Applies not to 4 alone. not binds more loosely than >, so it negates 4 > 9 (False) and gives True.
Confuses % with //. 17 // 5 is 3, but 17 % 5 is the remainder 2, so the comparison is True.

else if is the C/Java spelling. In Python, else must be followed directly by a colon, so else if x: is a SyntaxError.

Adds 0 + 1 + 2 + 3, treating range(1, 5) as if it were range(4).

why_wrong: Includes the stop value 0, but range stops before it even when counting down.

Skips the rest of the current loop iteration

why_wrong: That describes continue, which jumps to the next iteration. pass does not skip anything.
That describes break, which leaves the innermost loop.
pass has no effect on program flow. The next statement runs as normal.

range(5) stops before 5, so i never reaches 5.

Turns the falsy result of a and b into False; and returns the falsy operand itself, which is 0.

questions.q: In a lab, seats are numbered 1 to 40 and every row has 4 seats: seats 1-4 are row 1, seats 5-8 are row 2, and so on. Which expression gives the position of seat s inside its row (1, 2, 3 or 4)?

why_wrong: Gives 0 for seats 4, 8, 12 and so on, because a multiple of 4 leaves remainder 0.
Shifts every seat up by one: seat 1 gives 2 and seat 4 gives 1.
Adding before taking % moves the cycle the wrong way: seat 1 gives 2 and seat 3 gives 0.

print(x > 5 or x / 0, x < 5 and x / 0, x > 5 and x // 3)

In the last expression x > 5 is True, so and returns its second operand, x // 3 = 3, an int because // is floor division.
why_wrong: Assumes and returns True or False; when its first operand is truthy it returns the second operand itself, x // 3 = 3.
Treats // as true division; 10 // 3 is the int 3, while only 10 / 3 would give 3.3333333333333335.
Assumes both sides of and/or are always evaluated; short-circuiting means x / 0 is never reached in either expression.

why_wrong: For 2000, y % 100 != 0 and y % 400 != 0 are both False, so 2000 is rejected; it also accepts 1900, since 1900 % 400 != 0 is True.
and is evaluated before or, so this means y % 4 == 0 or (...); 1900 % 4 == 0 is True, so 1900 is wrongly accepted.
Requiring y % 100 != 0 for every year cancels the divisible-by-400 exception, so 2000 is rejected.

Treats // like /; floor division of two ints gives an int, so there is no .0.

Takes the outer else branch; 12 is even, so the outer if runs instead.

" " contains a space, so it is not empty and is truthy.
